description: The figure is a 3D bar chart illustrating model accuracy across different reasoning task types, with categories arranged on the horizontal plane and accuracy shown as bar height. One horizontal axis lists the models “Davinci-003,” “ChatGPT,” and “BARD” (shown along the left/front edge), and the other horizontal axis lists the task types “Inductive,” “Abductive,” “Deductive,” and “Mix” (shown along the right/front edge); no explicit scale type is indicated for these categorical axes. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy” and uses a linear numeric scale with tick labels at approximately 0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6, with bars extending to just under about 0.8. Each model–task combination is represented by a single rectangular bar colored with a blue-to-yellow gradient (blue near the base transitioning to green/yellow near the top), where taller bars appear more yellow at the top. For Davinci-003, the bars are approximately ~0.35 (Inductive), ~0.50 (Abductive), ~0.75 (Deductive), and ~0.75 (Mix). For ChatGPT, the bars are approximately ~0.20 (Inductive), ~0.35 (Abductive), ~0.50 (Deductive), and ~0.75 (Mix). For BARD, the bars are approximately ~0.45 (Inductive), ~0.40 (Abductive), ~0.70 (Deductive), and ~0.75 (Mix). The bars are displayed as a 3×4 grid (three models by four task types) with no stacking or grouping beyond their placement on the two categorical axes, and there are no visible annotations, outlines, or special emphasis; the ordering of categories follows the labeled sequences shown on the axes rather than an explicit sorted-by-value arrangement.
